findings.title: Expected cancellation is returned through the error channel
findings.reproduction: Return ControlFlow::Break from a round, unchecked-container or draw callback. The existing callback-cancellation tests exercise the production path.
findings.expected: CORE-22 requires a person's cancellation to be a returned outcome rather than an error.
findings.observed: The callbacks use ControlFlow, but each public operation translates Break to Err(Error::Cancelled). Fresh callback tests pass because they expect that error.
findings.impact: A consistent, documented API disagrees with the current error/outcome policy. This is not incorrect encryption, lost cleanup or an undocumented runtime regression.
findings.recommendedFix: Choose an explicit completion/cancellation outcome for the affected public operations and update callers, docs and bindings together. Treat this as an API change; coordinate with mhfe and wallet-tools before implementation.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise cancellation at each callback, before each round and during draw; require no result publication on cancellation and successful engine reuse. Compile affected native/browser consumers.

findings.title: The draw contract does not require a finite host trial budget
findings.reproduction: Read draw's public contract and loop. A correct rejection-sampling RNG may require more than any chosen finite number of trials; the stated average of 65,536 does not cap the loop.
findings.expected: CORE-50 requires a stated or person-selected bound for searches and batches. The library may delegate that bound to the host but must make the requirement explicit.
findings.observed: The fill callback can Break, but neither its contract nor a parameter requires a trial/time budget. The documentation bounds the passphrase, while the trial loop has only the statistical stopping condition.
findings.impact: A host can accidentally run an operation without a finite work budget. No practical exploit or incorrect output was demonstrated; this is a library-contract omission, not a defect in rejection sampling.
findings.recommendedFix: Require the host to establish a finite trial or time budget and return Break at exhaustion; document how the host distinguishes exhaustion from a person's cancellation. Preserve the profile's first-passing-trial semantics.
findings.requiredVerification: Use a bounded public fill callback and assert it stops at the exact configured count without returning a phrase. Check that a successful draw before exhaustion preserves the published profile result.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded standards, documentation or verification-tool defect; no current medium-or-higher runtime impact demonstrated.

findings.title: The historical stack-scan wrapper reports success after a build or probe failure
findings.reproduction: With a fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR, run run-matrix.sh invalid-profile CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=definitely-invalid. Cargo fails and no probe executable is produced. The retained command and log record script exit 0.
findings.expected: TOOL-02 and CORE-28 require a failed prerequisite, failed child or absent completed probe to prevent a successful verification verdict.
findings.observed: The script uses set -uo pipefail without errexit, ignores the build and timeout/probe statuses and returns only whether grep counted zero stack-hit lines. Failed execution produces no hit lines and passes.
findings.impact: A maintainer can accept a security check that never ran. This does not establish a current stack-erasure defect. AUD-004 separately built and ran the actual probe and checked its completed output.
evidence: Independent native and completeness source review
findings.recommendedFix: Provide a corrected, versioned wrapper that preserves build/probe failure and timeout, requires a completion marker and validates the expected control hits before interpreting absence of stack hits. Keep the historical failure evidence.
findings.requiredVerification: Require nonzero for invalid compiler profile, absent executable, probe crash, timeout, malformed/incomplete output and a positive stack-hit fixture; require zero for a completed clean scan.

findings.title: The README overstates the cost of every password guess
findings.reproduction: Compare the unqualified twelve-round cost for every attacker password guess with tests/spec/README.md:1234-1240 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:323-347.
findings.expected: DOC-07 requires the public cost claim to preserve the specification's known-pair caveat.
